note: Advice per rule id from privacy-scan RULES.md 1.2.0. kind: now = can be undone today (state), habit = change what you do from now on, permanent = the past stays on chain, info = nothing to do. who: anyone = anyone with a block explorer, exchange = the exchange behind the account, analysts = chain analysis firms with clustering tools. two actions rewritten as rules (deposit_address, timezone).

intro.title: Your fix plan
intro.lead: History on a public chain is permanent. This plan shows what you can change today, and what to do differently from now on.
intro.winBack: You can win back up to {points} points today.
intro.winBackNone: Nothing here can be undone today. The plan below keeps new links from forming.
intro.honest: A fix plan lowers what Nymra's rules can see. It does not make a wallet anonymous.

steps: Open the ENS App (app.ens.domains) with this wallet.
Next to Primary Name, choose Remove. It is one transaction on Ethereum.
Scan again and this finding is gone. Sites that already saw the name may still remember it.

public_identity.ens_records.action: Remove the records that point to you
steps: In the ENS App, open the name and edit its records.
Delete the records that lead to you: X, GitHub, email, website, Telegram, Discord, your real name.
Want to keep a public profile? Keep it on a wallet you use for nothing else.

public_identity.owned_names.action: Keep names on an identity wallet, and move private activity away from it
steps: Every ENS name this wallet owns shows up next to it on explorers.
Moving the names to another wallet would link that wallet to this one. Move your private activity to a fresh wallet instead, and let this one be your public identity.
An XNS name stays with its address for good. It cannot be removed or moved to another wallet.
Use this wallet for what you are happy to show under that name, and do private things from a fresh wallet.
An explorer or a public dataset already names this address. You cannot remove that label yourself.
Use this wallet only for what you are happy to show. Do private things from a fresh wallet.
This address is a smart contract. Scan the wallets that control it to see their exposure.

linked_wallets.back_and_forth.action: Stop sending directly between these wallets
steps: Every direct transfer between two wallets links them, in both directions.
Decide which wallets must stay apart, and never pay one from the other.
The links that exist stay on chain. Keep them from growing.

linked_wallets.funded_by_you.action: Do not fund new wallets from this one
steps: A new wallet whose first money came from you is linked to you from its first block.
Fund new wallets from a source that has never touched your other wallets. Follow the fresh wallet checklist.

linked_wallets.shared_deposit.action: Do not deposit from wallets you want kept apart into one exchange account
steps: An exchange gives each account its own deposit address. Two wallets paying into the same one look like one person.
Wallets that must stay apart should never pay into the same exchange account.

funding_reuse.shared_funder.action: Fund each new wallet from a different source, at a different time
steps: The wallet whose coins paid for your first transaction also sent coins to other new wallets within days. That pattern groups wallets together.
Next time, use one source per wallet and spread funding over days, not minutes.
On several chains, your first transaction was paid with coins from the same wallet. That ties your activity there together.
If chains should stay apart, use a different address on each, funded separately.
What paid for your first transaction came from a busy service or bot. That hides you in a crowd, but the service itself may know who you are.
Your funder paid no other new wallet around that time. Keep funding wallets one source at a time.

cex_exposure.funded_by_cex.action: Assume your exchange can see this wallet
steps: Your first transaction on this chain was paid with coins from an exchange. The exchange knows which account withdrew them.
That link is permanent. For a wallet that must stay private, do not withdraw to it straight from an exchange account in your name.

cex_exposure.direct.action: Keep exchange transfers on one public wallet
steps: Transfers with exchange wallets show that this wallet is a customer.
Use one wallet for exchange deposits and withdrawals, and keep private wallets away from it.

cex_exposure.deposit_address.action: Pay this deposit address only from this wallet
steps: Exchanges give each customer their own deposit address, so this one very likely belongs to your verified account.
Every wallet that ever pays into it is linked to that account. Do not deposit from wallets you want kept apart.

cross_chain.multichain_presence.action: Use another address where you want a separate history
steps: The same address on many chains shows one history everywhere.
Your seed phrase gives you as many addresses as you want. Use a different one per chain or per purpose.

cross_chain.bridge_match.action: Bridge to a different address, and not the exact amount
steps: An amount left one chain and almost the same amount arrived here within minutes. That joins the two trails.
Bridge to another address, and do not move everything on in one go.
Others sent coins or tokens to this address on chains you never used. Anyone can send to any address, so this is not your trail and costs no points.
Leave tokens you did not expect alone: some exist only to get you to sign something. Sending from such a chain makes it part of your trail.

behavioral_fingerprint.timezone.action: Send at different hours of the day
steps: You almost never transact during the night of one time zone. That narrows down where you live.
The past stays. Sending some transactions at other hours blurs the pattern from now on.

behavioral_fingerprint.round_amounts.action: Send amounts that are not round
steps: Round amounts like 0.5, 1 or 100 are easy to match across wallets and chains.
When the exact amount does not matter, send 0.4837 instead of 0.5.

behavioral_fingerprint.fixed_gas.action: Let your wallet set the gas
steps: One exact gas setting on many transactions is a signature, often of a script.
Use your wallet's normal gas estimate instead of a fixed custom value.
Transactions at a fixed interval look like automation and are easy to recognize.
If a script sends for you, give it random delays.

behavioral_fingerprint.wallet_software.action: Switch back to a standard account if you do not need smart features
steps: This address delegates to a smart account (EIP-7702), which shows which wallet app you use.
If you do not need its features, switch back to a standard account in your wallet's settings. Not every wallet supports this yet.

recurring_counterparties.top.action: Use separate wallets for separate relationships
steps: A few addresses make up most of your transfers. That small circle is easy to recognize.
Keep payroll, friends and trading on different wallets.

freshWallet.title: Start clean: a fresh wallet checklist

steps.do: Make a new address. A new account in your wallet is enough; never reuse an address you have shared.
steps.why: A new address starts with no history.

steps.do: Do not set a primary ENS name or records on it.
steps.why: A name is the fastest way from an address to a person.

steps.do: Fund it from a source that has never touched your other wallets.
steps.why: Where the coins for a first transaction came from is the first thing anyone checks.

steps.do: Send amounts that are not round, at different times of day.
steps.why: Round amounts and fixed hours are easy to match.

steps.do: Never send between this wallet and your main wallet.
steps.why: One direct transfer links them for good.

steps.do: Bridge to another address, not the same one.
steps.why: The same address on every chain is one trail.

steps.do: Scan it with Compare against your main wallet before you use it.
steps.why: Nymra checks whether its rules can already link the two.

freshWallet.honest: This checklist lowers what Nymra's rules can see. It does not make a wallet anonymous, and it is not legal advice.
